objective: Map (goal, world, constraints, uncertainty) to an adequate action with minimum decision-changing information, verified execution, and independent actual-goal acceptance.

closure_law.statement: For any two admissible world states w1 and w2 that remain indistinguishable under all authenticated observations available to the decision process, a universally adequate controller exists only if their adequate-action sets intersect (including a safe defer/abstain action when that itself satisfies the goal). If the adequate-action sets are disjoint, some authenticated observation capable of separating the states is information-theoretically necessary.
closure_law.consequence: The correct general algorithm is not to guess missing semantics or build a complete world model. It is to preserve the raw goal losslessly, maintain sound uncertainty, acquire only policy-changing discriminators, authenticate policy adequacy, bind the selected policy to execution, execute, and independently verify actual goal satisfaction. When a required discriminator is unavailable, the only truthful result is the exact unresolved edge.

sufficient_solution.execution_rule: NO_POLICY_SELECTION_GRANTS_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY; EXECUTION_REQUIRES AN AUTHENTICATED POLICY_TO_EXECUTION BINDING AND VERIFIED EFFECTS.
sufficient_solution.verification_rule: EXECUTION_SUCCESS_IS_NOT GOAL SUCCESS; ACTUAL GOAL SATISFACTION MUST BE INDEPENDENTLY CONTENT_BOUND_AND VERIFIED.
sufficient_solution.extension_rule: NEW SEMANTICS, SOURCES, POLICIES, OR CAPABILITIES ENTER ONLY AS ZERO_AUTHORITY CANDIDATES AND MUST REENTER THE EXISTING VERIFICATION KERNEL.

remaining_boundary.meaning: These are coverage/observability boundaries. They cannot be eliminated by a better decision rule alone. Each reached boundary must be closed by adding authenticated evidence, a valid discriminator, a common robust action, or a verified capability.
